name: AI Alt Text Builder – Alt Text Generator for Image SEO & Accessibility
author: RankPilotAI

sections.description:
AI Alt Text Builder writes accurate, descriptive alt text for the images in your Media Library, in one click or in bulk.

Images without alt text cost you twice. Search engines cannot tell what the image shows, so it ranks lower in Google Images, and screen reader users hear nothing at all. Accessibility standards such as WCAG 2.1, which both the ADA Title II rule in the US and the European Accessibility Act in the EU build on, require a text alternative for every meaningful image.

Start free in seconds: 25 free generations, no sign-up and no API key. Prefer your own OpenAI API key? Then single-image generations are unlimited, and you only pay OpenAI’s usage.

Fixing hundreds of images? Pro writes alt text for your whole Media Library in bulk and can fill it in automatically on every new upload. Plans start at $2.99/month, billed yearly. See pricing

Highlights

  • Works instantly – no registration required, 25 free tokens on first use
  • BYOK mode – use your own OpenAI API key for unlimited single image generations
  • One-click “Generate with AI” button on Media Library items and the attachment edit screen
  • Automatically saves to _wp_attachment_image_alt
  • Built-in ALT-length score badge (0-100) and a sortable Media Library column, so missing or weak alt text is easy to find
  • Works with every image in the Media Library, including WooCommerce product images, and with any theme, page builder or SEO plugin
  • Pro: Bulk generation, auto-generate on upload, all languages, all models, custom prompts
  • Language selector (English, Deutsch, Francais, Espanol, Turkce, or custom)
  • Three quality tiers: Economical, Balanced, Premium

External services

This plugin connects to RankPilotAI’s API to generate ALT text and to fetch token status.

What is sent and when

  • Trial mode: Site URL is sent to RankPilotAI for registration. Image URL is sent to RankPilotAI for processing.
  • BYOK mode: Image URL is sent directly to OpenAI’s API using your own API key. Nothing is sent to RankPilotAI.
  • Pro mode: Image URL, file name, current ALT, selected model, language, site URL, domain, plugin slug, and Site Token are sent to RankPilotAI.
  • On token-status checks in the settings page (Pro mode only): Site Token, site URL and domain.

Why it is sent

  • To generate the requested ALT text and return it to your Media Library item
  • To authorize usage and show your remaining balance (Pro mode)
  • To register and track trial token usage (Trial mode)

Endpoints

  • https://rankpilotai.com/wp-json/rankpilotai/v1/alt-text (Pro)
  • https://rankpilotai.com/wp-json/rankpilotai/v1/alt-batch (Pro bulk)
  • https://rankpilotai.com/wp-json/rankpilotai/v1/token-info (Pro)
  • https://rankpilotai.com/wp-json/rankpilotai/v1/trial-register (Trial)
  • https://rankpilotai.com/wp-json/rankpilotai/v1/trial-alt (Trial)
  • https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions (BYOK – direct to OpenAI)

Providers

  • RankPilotAI (Terms: https://rankpilotai.com/terms-and-conditions, Privacy: https://rankpilotai.com/privacy-policy)
  • Anthropic (Claude API): in Trial and Pro mode the RankPilotAI API passes the image URL and the instruction prompt to Anthropic to generate the ALT text. Terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms, Privacy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • OpenAI: used by the RankPilotAI API as an automatic fallback when Anthropic is unavailable, and called directly from your site in BYOK mode. Terms: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use, Privacy: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy
sections.installation:
1. Upload and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to AI Alt Text Builder in the admin menu.
  3. Choose your mode:
    • Free Trial – Click “Start Free Trial” for 25 free tokens (no registration needed)
    • Own API Key – Enter your OpenAI API key for unlimited single image generations
    • Pro – Enter your RankPilotAI Site Key for full features
  4. Open Media → Library or an attachment and click Generate with AI.
sections.faq:
Do I need to register or create an account?

No. The free trial starts instantly with one click. For BYOK mode, just paste your OpenAI API key.

Is there a free plan?

Yes. 25 free tokens are included. After that, use your own OpenAI API key (unlimited, free) or upgrade to Pro.

Does it overwrite my existing ALT texts?

Only when you click Generate for a given image (or run a bulk action). It writes to WordPress’ standard _wp_attachment_image_alt field.

What languages are supported?

English, German, French, Spanish, Turkish — plus Other/Custom. Enter any language name and we’ll pass it to the generator.

Will it change image file names or titles?

No. It only sets the ALT text and stores a score _aatb_score meta (for the badge/column).

Does it work with other media/SEO plugins?

Yes. ALT text is a core WordPress field, so other plugins and themes will read it normally.

Does alt text help SEO?

Yes. Search engines read alt text to understand what an image shows, which helps the image appear in Google Images and gives the page more relevant context. Good alt text describes the image in plain words; it is not a place to stuff keywords, and the generator does not do that.

Does it help with accessibility compliance (WCAG, ADA, European Accessibility Act)?

It fills the text alternative that WCAG success criterion 1.1.1 asks for on meaningful images, which is one of the most common failures in accessibility audits. It does not make a whole site compliant on its own: other WCAG criteria, such as colour contrast and keyboard access, still apply.

Can I generate alt text for all my existing images at once?

Yes, with Pro. Bulk generation works through your Media Library images in batches, and auto-generate fills in alt text for every new upload. The free trial and BYOK mode generate one image at a time.
sections.changelog:
1.0.21

  • Improved: bulk generation now goes image by image, three at a time, in the Media Library grid and list view, so the counter moves with every image (“1 / 3”, “2 / 3”) instead of jumping from 0 to the end.
  • Improved: in the list view, Apply on “Generate with AI Alt Text Builder” starts at once with a progress bar and a Stop button, without reloading the page. Each row’s Alt Text label changes as its text arrives.
  • Improved: when a bulk job ends, the images that got alt text are deselected (unticked in the list), so the button cannot be pressed for them again by mistake. Images that failed, or were not reached because of Stop, stay selected for another try.
  • Improved: the list view’s alt text filter now uses the states of the Alt Text column: Missing, Too short, Good and Too long. It lists images only (a PDF or a video has no alt text) and has a label for screen readers.
  • Fix: the Alternative Text box grows with its text. On WordPress 7, the last line of a typical alt text was cut off.

1.0.20

  • Fix: in the Media Library grid, bulk generation could lose the new alt text of the last image you selected: when you left Bulk select, WordPress saved that image’s old, empty field back over it. Every generated alt text now stays.
  • Fix: Stop now stops bulk generation, in the list view and in the grid. Before, a Stop pressed while images were being processed (or, in the grid, right after clicking Generate) was lost and the job ran to the end, using tokens for every selected image. Now only the images already in progress are finished.
  • Fix: moving to another image while one image’s alt text was being generated, followed by a failed generation, removed that image’s previous alt text. It now stays.
  • Improved: the bulk result line is the same in the grid and the list view, with the right singular or plural (“1 alt text saved.”).

1.0.19

  • Fix: in the Media Library grid, the result line next to “Generate alt text (N)” (for example “2 alt texts saved, 0 failed”) now lines up vertically with the toolbar buttons.

1.0.18

  • New: the Generate button now also appears in the “Attachment details” window, which opens when you click an image in the Media Library grid or pick one in the editor’s media window. Before, it was only on the separate attachment edit screen.
  • New: a “Generate alt text (N)” button in the Media Library grid view. Click Bulk select, pick images and generate alt text for all of them, with a progress bar and a Stop button. Before, bulk generation was only reachable from the list view’s Bulk actions menu.
  • Improved: the Generate control now uses the standard WordPress button style. Clicking it clears the field and shows “Generating…” until the new alt text arrives; once an image has alt text, the button reads “Regenerate”. If generation fails, the previous text is put back.
  • Improved: the “100 / 100” score is replaced by a clear label (Missing, Too short, Good, Too long) and a character count, in the field and in the Media Library column (now named “Alt Text”).
  • Improved: a calmer settings screen in the WordPress admin style. The model cards now show the quality tiers (Economical, Balanced, Premium) with their token cost, the screen says which AI service generates the text, and Pro users no longer see the mode comparison table.
  • Security: the site key is masked on the settings screen; “Change site key” opens an empty field instead of showing the current key.
  • Accessibility: progress and result messages are announced to screen readers, and the settings screen buttons use the WordPress admin button styles with a visible keyboard focus.
  • Security: generating alt text, for one image or in bulk, now also checks that the user may edit that specific image.
  • Improved: the list view’s bulk progress now shows a progress bar, “Generating alt text for N images…” and a Stop button, and ends with one clear result message instead of “processed 0/0 – success 0, failed 0”.
  • Fix: stopping a bulk job from the list view no longer stays on “cancelling…”.

1.0.17

  • Fix: when the RankPilotAI API answered with a structured error object (for example {"error":{"message":"..."}}) instead of a plain string, generating ALT text ended in a server error and the real reason never reached you. The message inside the object is now shown. This extends the 1.0.16 trial fix to the Site Key path.
  • Maintenance: replaced the deprecated jQuery.trim() (removed in jQuery 4) in the ALT score badge with the native String.prototype.trim(). The score is calculated exactly as before.
  • Compatibility: verified on WordPress 7.1.3 with PHP 8.5. The official Plugin Check reports zero errors, and the Media Library (list and grid), the attachment and post editors and the settings screen load without a single PHP notice or deprecation.

1.0.16

  • Fix: removed a PHP warning (“Undefined array key”) that the plugin raised every time WordPress built the attachment fields, which is on every media modal open. WordPress does not define an html key for the alternative text field, and the plugin appended to it without checking. On sites that display PHP notices, the warning could leak into the media modal response.
  • Hardening: if the trial API returns a structured error object instead of a string, the request no longer ends in a fatal error; the message is shown to you instead.
  • Maintenance: the plugin now passes the official WordPress Plugin Check with zero errors. This covers output escaping, translator comments on every placeholder string, wp_parse_url(), and prepared uninstall queries. Where a check does not apply, the exemption is documented inline with its reason rather than left silent.
  • Compatibility: verified on a real WordPress 7.1 install, including the Media Library list table, the media modal and the post editor.

1.0.15

  • NEW: the Alt Score column in the Media Library is now sortable, as the description has always claimed. Empty ALT text sorts as 0, matching the badge.
  • Fix: the “Generate with AI” button inside the media modal no longer appears without the script that powers it. The button used to render on any screen that opens the modal, while its JavaScript only loaded on the Media Library and attachment screens, so clicking it did nothing.
  • Fix: files the vision models cannot read (SVG, HEIC, AVIF and similar) are now rejected up front with a clear message instead of consuming a token on a request that was going to fail. WordPress 7.1 lets the browser convert and generate files before upload, so the Media Library can hold more formats than before.
  • Hardening: request values are unslashed before sanitizing, and the uninstall cleanup query is now prepared with esc_like().
  • Compatibility: tested with WordPress 7.1.

1.0.14

  • Maintenance: added the missing “Plugin URI” header and translated remaining inline code comments to English.
  • Compatibility: re-verified with WordPress 7.0.
